title: Mötley Crüe Plots 4th Las Vegas Residency Featuring Songs That Haven’t Been Played Live ‘In Decades’

title: Selena Gomez Laments How Nicotine Vaping ‘Changed’ Her Voice: ‘It’s So Stupid’
summary: The 34-year-old singer told fans in a Story that vaping is very hard to quit and that it's "not worth it."
body: Selena Gomez has always made a point of being very honest with her fans. Which is why it was not surprising that in a candid Instagram Story post on Sunday (Oct. 18), the 34-year-old singer got real about the negative effects of vaping nicotine has had on her voice. “I’m not gonna be able to change my voice,” she said in the post . “I vaped nicotine a lot … Nicotine is so hard to quit, and I think I just wanted to say, if you’re going through it, or if you’re even trying to vape, it’s just not worth it. It’s so stupid, and it’s changed my voice.” The singer said that if fans don’t like hearing her voice it’s totally fine. “Just don’t listen to it. Just don’t listen,” she suggested. The good news is that Gomez said she’s excited because she’s stopped vaping. “I just hope that I can keep it up,” she added before giving her fans a positive affirmation to hold onto. “If you are going through something, you can get through it too. It sucks.” According to the Cleveland Clinic , among the dangers of vaping are addiction to nicotine, asthma, cancer, lung scarring, coughing, shortness of b…

title: Spotify is cracking down on Family plan sharing, but you can still bypass the checks
summary: The streaming platform is using dynamic QR codes to enforce household rules this time.
body: Credit: Ryan Haines / Android Authority TL;DR Spotify is cracking down on Family plan sharing by requiring members to complete dynamic QR code address scans in person. Unverified users have seven days to complete the scan or face demotion to the Free tier and a 12-month ban on joining shared Family or Duo plans. Screenshots aren’t feasible with these dynamic QR codes, so subscribers are sidestepping the check by screen-sharing across multiple devices. Spotify is stepping up enforcement of its household location rules, leaving several Premium Family plan subscribers suddenly booted off their shared plans. The streaming giant is cracking down on family plan sharing to ensure that all members reside at the same location as the plan manager. A growing number of Reddit users are reporting that Spotify Family plan account holders are receiving sudden address re-verification prompts, particularly if they are not at the same location as other users on the Family plan. This re-verification is seemingly being done in person, with constantly refreshing QR code scans between the plan manager’s device and the member’s phone to confirm they live in the same household.

The placing matches their previous best with 2011’s Idols and 2013’s Brand New Machine . title: The best PS3 emulator on Android just got a massive local multiplayer upgrade
summary: ARMSX3 now offers the equivalent of Nintendo's Download Play on Android devices.
body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority TL;DR ARMSX3 now lets you play local multiplayer games with a friend over the same Wi-Fi network or online. The friend is player two and can play with their own controller or touch controls. This feature doesn’t require the second player to have their own copy of a game. ARMSX3 is the top PlayStation 3 emulator on Android, having received a steady stream of updates since its release earlier this year. One update in August brought online multiplayer functionality, but a recent update brings a major upgrade for local multiplayer. ARMSX3 v1.2 was released a few days ago, and the app now supports remote local multiplayer functionality. That is, you can play as player two in a friend’s multiplayer game streamed over the same Wi-Fi network or online.

title: iPhone Duo battery specs revealed: Good news for Galaxy Z Fold 8 and other Android rivals
summary: iPhone batteries are yet to break the "1,000 charging cycles" barrier.
body: TL;DR The iPhone Duo has a 4,883mAh battery according to EU regulatory labels. It’s also rated for 1,000 charging cycles before dropping to 80% capacity. The Galaxy Z Fold 8’s 4,660mAh battery, on the other hand, is rated for 1,200 charging cycles. Apple recently opened preorders for the iPhone Duo. While everyone is talking about the folding-and-unfolding animation or the clever hinge-based cooling design , the EU released some information about the iPhone Duo’s battery worth noting. The European Union’s energy label database finally has information about the iPhone Duo’s battery (via MacRumors ). According to the EU’s regulatory database, the iPhone Duo packs a 4,883mAh battery.

body: Kings of Leon will tour Australia in February and March 2027, playing outdoor shows in Sydney, Brisbane and Melbourne with Australian band Ocean Alley as special guests. The run opens in Auckland and follows the Nov. 6 release of their 10th studio album, O My Beloved . The Sydney show is their headline slot at Sydney Summertime on Sunday, Feb. 28, with the new outdoor concert series at Centennial Park run by Black Peach . The series previously announced The Strokes as its first headliner for Feb. 20, with Beck, Courtney Barnett and Promiseland, making Kings of Leon the second international headliner. More headliners are set to be announced in the coming months. From there, the band plays Brisbane Showgrounds on Wednesday, March 3, and Flemington Racecourse in Melbourne on Friday, March 5, after opening at Live at The Domain in Auckland on Wednesday, Feb. 24. The dates skip Adelaide and Perth. The tour follows a stripped-back turn for the Followill family band, brothers Caleb, Nathan and Jared and cousin Matthew. title: Pixel 11 Pro XL vs. Galaxy S27 Ultra: Why you shouldn’t buy Google’s flagship right now
summary: My Pixel crush has commitment issues.
body: I got my hands on the Google Pixel 11 Pro XL when it launched globally in August, and I’ve spent quite a bit of time with it since. It’s not my daily driver, but I’ve used it enough to know what I love about it and, more importantly, where I wish Google had done things differently. If there’s one thing I’ve come to appreciate about Pixel phones over the years, it’s how Google gets so many of the little things right. From the design and software to how everything feels in everyday use, using a Pixel has a certain charm that’s hard to ignore. Of course, that doesn’t mean everything is perfect. Performance is still one area where I’d love to see Google step things up, especially when you look at what the competition has to offer. And with Samsung’s Galaxy S27 Ultra expected to arrive early next year , that gap could become even more noticeable.

title: This watchmaker has reportedly exited the smartwatch market
summary: The Connected Calibre E5 looks to be the brand’s last.
body: TL;DR TAG Heuer reportedly ended production of its Connected smartwatches over the summer. There is no word on how long its smartwatches will get software updates or service. The move comes as screenless fitness trackers become more popular. Smartwatches deliver a constant stream of information to our wrists, but one thing they’re not always clued in about is their own demise. Screenless fitness trackers , smart rings, and even smart glasses are taking over facets of their job. News that TAG Heuer has quietly exited the smartwatch game is the latest sign that traditional smartwatches are becoming more scarce. French publication La Lettre reports that TAG Heuer ceased production of its Connected smartwatches over the summer (via Notebookcheck ). It said that remaining stock will be sold off through 2027, and that there is no word on how long existing smartwatches will receive software updates or service.

title: Hate the idea of paying for YouTube Premium? Imagine paying $240 a year for regular YouTube
summary: YouTube's next big fee might not even come from Google.
body: TL;DR The UK government is considering expanding its annual £180 (~$240) TV license fee to cover on-demand streaming services like YouTube, Netflix, and Disney Plus. If implemented, the change could require households to pay a license fee even to watch regular YouTube videos, without getting any Premium benefits. The proposal aims to address declining BBC funding but hasn’t been finalized. Does nothing sound worse than the idea of paying for YouTube Premium ? Well, imagine having to pay the government just for getting access to regular YouTube with none of the Premium perks attached. Sounds ridiculous, right? Unfortunately, that’s a possibility under consideration in the UK. To truly understand the development, you first need to understand the concept of a TV license fee in the UK. By law, you must have a TV license (£180 per year/~$240) if you plan on watching or recording programs as they’re being shown on live TV. You also need a license if you plan on watching or streaming programs live on online TV services, including the likes of YouTube, Netflix, and even Amazon Prime Video. You do not need a license if you’re only watching on-demand content on these platforms, like our lat…

title: MapQuest’s new tool can help you avoid Flock cameras
summary: The terrifyingly informative new map layer reveals all the cameras around you.
body: TL;DR MapQuest is enjoying some fresh attention thanks to its pushback against a few of 2026’s worst trends. After resisting politically charged renaming efforts, it’s now giving users a way to see surveillance cameras. The new Surveillance Layer reveals Flock cameras, as well as similar solutions from multiple other brands. Is life in 2026 feeling sufficiently dystopian for you? Between increasingly advanced AI causing us to stress about everything from our jobs to component prices , and the rise of far-right governments around the world, this is definitely not the utopian paradise you might have been hoping for. But from all that horrible mess, one savior has emerged to offer a beacon of hope — just who would have ever thought it would be MapQuest? MapQuest was great at helping us getting around… 20 years ago, before Google Maps arrived, anyway. And just like so many other turn-of-the-century dot coms, it quickly found itself fading into the background.

title: Android Auto’s missing signal bars are finally making a proper comeback
summary: A wider rollout is restoring the vanished cell network connectivity icon to in-car displays.
body: Credit: Shimul Sood / Android Authority TL;DR Google is expanding the rollout of a fix that restores the missing network signal icon in Android Auto. The issue began months ago when an update removed the icon, leaving drivers unable to view cell reception status on their car screens. The fix seems to rely on a mix of app updates and server-side flags, so a full rollout across all devices may still take weeks. If you have been driving blind to your phone’s cellular connectivity, relief is finally rolling out. Google appears to be widening the rollout of a fix that restores the missing network signal icon in Android Auto , addressing a frustrating bug that left drivers guessing whether their phone actually had reception. Over the past few days, multiple users on Reddit have reported that the network icon is back on their in-car displays, as mysteriously as it disappeared in the first place. Drivers with different vehicle infotainment setups and phone models are seeing the familiar status indicator rejoin the battery and Wi-Fi icons in the status bar.

title: The Galaxy S27 Plus could break nearly six years of tradition with this downgrade
summary: The potential downgrade reaches beyond finding your misplaced keys.
body: TL;DR Chinese regulatory filings suggest the Galaxy S27 Plus could drop UWB, a feature Plus models have offered since the S21 Plus. That could mean losing more precise tracking and hands-free access to compatible cars and smart locks, although some alternatives would remain. The apparent Pro and Ultra listings include UWB, but Samsung hasn’t confirmed the lineup’s final specifications. Samsung gave its phones a useful sense of direction when it introduced ultra-wideband (UWB) on the Galaxy Note 20 Ultra. The technology promised easier ways to find belongings and the ability to unlock compatible cars without reaching for your phone. Now, the Galaxy S27 Plus could lose that hardware, breaking a streak that began with the S21 Plus. According to leaker Abhishek Yadav on X , Chinese MIIT certifications list UWB for the Galaxy S27 Pro and S27 Ultra, but omit it from the Galaxy S27 and S27 Plus. That would be business as usual for the base model, since Samsung has consistently left UWB out of its standard Galaxy S phones. It would, however, mark an unexpected downgrade for the Plus after years of support. But these filings don’t establish Samsung’s final global specifications, so the rem…

title: Your next ePaper tablet will feel a lot more colorful, lot less like a faded newspaper
summary: E Ink's new Kaleido 4 displays are far more saturated, offer better visibility, and allow smoother page turning than ever.
body: Credit: E Ink TL;DR E Ink just announced its new Kaleido 4 display technology with support for a wider color gamut. In addition to the colors, the new display offers 50% better contrast. Hanvon Technology’s M10C II is the first ePaper tablet with this display. E Ink’s Kaleido line is considered the gold standard for colored ePaper displays . Kaleido displays are found on leading e-readers from brands such as Amazon, BOOX, Kobo, and others. Building on this, E Ink has now launched Kaleido 4 with richer color, snappier page refreshes, and display quality that leads to a “more detailed and fluid ePaper experience.” In its press note, E Ink says the new Kaleido 4 displays are now suitable for a wider variety of digital content. According to the announcement, the latest version supports a color gamut twice as large, with a volume exceeding 40,000. That does not mean 40,000 colors, but without a unit associated, it’s difficult to make objective sense of the number than just saying that the display will now deliver more saturated colors than before.

title: I wouldn’t buy these phones, and neither should you
summary: There are five phones I wouldn't touch for specific reasons.
body: I’m the Shallow Hal of Android fandom. I wouldn’t touch certain Android phones with a ten-foot pole if they have a specific trait I don’t like. I’m not talking about smartphones with overwhelmingly negative reviews . In fact, there are a few poorly reviewed products I take a fancy to . I’m referring to smartphones that have one or two deal-breakers, in spite of their positive first impressions. It could be as trivial as a missing feature, or more unforgivable like a substantial price hike. Whichever it may be, I’d rather save my money for something else.

title: I ignored this Google Maps feature for 10 years, and now I can’t live without it
summary: No more digging through messages for forgotten addresses.
body: As a person with no sense of direction, I’ve been using Google Maps to get around since the app was first available for my smartphone. Even when I can’t mount my phone to my car dashboard, I use its audio navigation to guide me to destinations I’m not familiar with. But as the app has rolled out newer features, I’ve had a habit of ignoring them. My You tab remains neglected, and I’ve only ever left two reviews (both seven years ago) in the app. I also happily ignore the recommendations that appear when I’m about to search for something. However, recently I decided to revisit the lists and labeled places features — and realized that I’ve been missing out.

body: I tested Google’s first smart home controller designed for the Gemini era, the Google Home Speaker , more than three months ago. I hoped the Home Speaker would usher in a new wave of Google smart home products, but the opposite has happened in the time since. The Nest Audio and Nest Mini were discontinued, and the second-generation Nest Hub and the Nest Hub Max are both out of stock on the Google Store. title: Sony just proved that ‘three OS updates’ doesn’t really mean anything
summary: Sony needs to offer a much stronger explanation for this.
body: TL;DR Sony has decided not to roll out the Android 17 update to the Xperia 10 VI. The company says it’s due to “technical limitations” of the Xperia 10 VI’s storage configuration. The Xperia 10 VI was promised three OS updates at launch, implying that it would be upgraded to Android 17. Sony started rolling out Android 17 to its flagship Xperia 1 VIII early last month. At the same time, the company released a list of phones eligible for the update, which surprisingly did not include the Xperia 10 VI. While that raised doubts about Sony’s plans for the phone, we now know that it’s simply never getting Android 17 . In a notice posted on its website, Sony confirmed that the Xperia 10 VI, released in 2024, will not be updated to Android 17. According to the company, “technical limitations due to the device’s storage configuration” prevent it from offering an Android 17 experience that Sony considers adequate.

title: Google reminds Android users of an overlooked scam detection tool
summary: Circle to Search and Google Lens can also help you detect scams!
body: TL;DR Google is highlighting Circle to Search’s existing ability to identify suspicious text messages using AI Overviews. We tested the functionality, and it works as intended, with Google explaining why a message might be fraudulent and suggesting next steps. Google Lens offers the same scam-checking functionality on phones without Circle to Search, including iPhones. Google’s suite of scam detection features is great at filtering out suspicious messages and calls before you fall for them. The tech giant has been steadily improving the collection and rolling it out to more users, though that’s also the big catch here. Not all scam detection features are available on every Android phone. Newer developments, like enhanced protection mode in Google Messages , are available on even fewer devices. With the company announcing new tools, it’s worth revisiting an existing one that’s available to a much wider range of users and devices. Google is highlighting that scam detection is available via Circle to Search (CtS) , giving a larger subset of users who don’t have scam detection natively access to preventive tools that can help them avoid falling victim to fraud.

title: ANBERNIC is quietly removing a controversial extra from its Android handhelds
summary: The company is dropping microSD card bundle options just days after facing accusations of distributing pirated games.
body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority TL;DR ANBERNIC has started removing optional microSD card bundles from several handheld listings on its official store. The changes follow an ESA complaint accusing ANBERNIC of selling devices bundled with unauthorized games. ANBERNIC hasn’t confirmed a connection, but the move may be intended to head off further action against the company. ANBERNIC has had quite a week. After recently unveiling its Nintendo 3DS-inspired RG DDS handheld — whose potential pricing was leaked earlier today — the company found itself facing scrutiny over the copyrighted games allegedly bundled with its devices. Within days of the complaint coming to light, ANBERNIC now appears to be quietly removing the contentious microSD card options from its online store. As spotted by Retro Handhelds , several ANBERNIC handheld listings have lost the option to purchase additional microSD cards alongside the devices. The publication compared an archived version of the RG SP listing from August 14 with the current storefront, finding that only the 16GB option remains. That card is still needed because it contains the handheld’s stock firmware.

body: TL;DR Android’s Earthquake Alerts System is expanding to more regions: 200+, up from 98. Be Ready earthquake alert notifications will be getting an update “in the coming months.” Google says Android has delivered more than a billion individual earthquake alerts since 2021. Android’s built-in earthquake alerts are expanding to a lot more places. Google’s announced that the system that’s been available in 98 countries and regions to date is now available in more than 200. The alerts themselves are getting an upgrade, too. Google made the announcements in a blog post that wraps up a handful of earthquake alert updates. The post says that the new regions where earthquake alerts are now available includes Panama and Guatemala, though as of publication, the feature’s support documentation hasn’t yet been updated to include the full list.
